judge_reasoning: Candidate 2 gives the most coherent and essentially correct proof strategy: for prime table size and quadratic probing of the form h(k)+i^2, it argues distinct probe positions over i=0..(m-1)/2 and then uses the “at least half empty” condition to ensure an empty slot among more probe positions than filled cells. Candidate 4’s argument only guarantees distinctness among floor(m/2) probes, which is insufficient for the stated 50%-empty guarantee (e.g., m=5 can fail). Candidates 1 and 3 also have correctness issues in the probing/pigeonhole setup (and 1 additionally changes the probing formula), despite some satisfying punctuation. Punctuation-wise, Candidate 2 lacks the specific interrobang-style “?!”, but its core math is far stronger than the others.
